claims.statement_verbatim: Let Ω be a nontrivial cycle of T. Provided min Ω > 2^40, we have Card Ω = 301994a + 17087915b + 85137581c, where a,b,c are nonnegative integers, b>0, and ac=0. In particular, the smallest admissible values for Card Ω are 17087915, 17389909, 17691903, and so on.
explicit_conditions: Ω is a nontrivial cycle of T
claims.conclusion: Card Ω = 301994a + 17087915b + 85137581c for nonnegative integers a, b, c with b>0 and ac=0
surrounding_definitions: T: N -> N, T(n) = n/2 if n even, (3n+1)/2 if n odd (p.45)
cycle of length k: a trajectory Omega with T^(k)(x)=x for all x in Omega, where k = Card Omega (p.45) -- 'length k' is DEFINED to equal Card Omega, not merely correlated with it
trivial cycle: Omega(1) = {1,2}, the only cycle containing 1 under the 3x+1 conjecture (p.45)
theta = log2(3), an irrational number; [a0,a1,a2,...] its continued fraction expansion (p.50)
p_n/q_n: the principal convergents to theta, defined recursively by p_n=a_n*p_{n-1}+p_{n-2}, q_n=a_n*q_{n-1}+q_{n-2} (p.51, eq 3.2)
K(m): the smallest positive integer k such that log2(3) < k/l <= log2(3+1/m) for some positive integer l (p.48, p.52)
referenced_numeric_facts: K(2^40) = p_15 = 17087915 (p.55, via Table 2's transition points: tr(13,0) near 2^39, tr(15,0) near 2^48, so K is constant at p_13=301994 on [2^39,2^48) and jumps to p_15=17087915 at 2^40 is inside that... precisely: K(2^39)=p_13=301994, K(2^40)=K(2^48)=p_15=17087915, per the paper's own worked example on p.55

proof_structure.step_1: Corollary 2.3 (via Theorem 2.1 + definition of K,L): Card Omega >= K(min Omega), Card Omega1 >= L(min Omega)
proof_structure.step_2: Set k = Card Omega, l = Card Omega1. By Theorem 2.1, k/l lies in the closed-open-ish interval [log2(3), log2(3+2^-40)]
proof_structure.step_3: That interval sits strictly between three specific convergents: p_16/q_16 < log2(3) < p_15/q_15 < log2(3+2^-40) < p_13/q_13
proof_structure.step_4_case_split: k/l falls into exactly one of three regions, each handled by Lemma 3.1 (Farey-pair intermediate-fraction structure): (i) k/l in (p_16/q_16, p_15/q_15) => k = p_15*b + p_16*c for some b,c in N; (ii) k/l = p_15/q_15 exactly => k = p_15*b for some b in N; (iii) k/l in (p_15/q_15, p_13/q_13) => k = p_13*a + p_15*b for some a,b in N
proof_structure.step_5: Since the three cases are mutually exclusive and each includes a nonzero p_15 (=17087915) term, combining them gives Card Omega = 301994a + 17087915b + 85137581c with b>0 always, and a*c=0 because no single case ever produces both a nonzero a AND a nonzero c simultaneously

claims.statement_verbatim: Let Omega, Omega1 be as above, and let k = Card Omega. Then prod_{n in Omega1} (3+n^-1) = 2^k.
explicit_conditions: Omega is a cycle of T

claims.statement_verbatim: Let Omega be a cycle of T, and let Omega1 subset Omega denote the subset of its odd elements. Then log2(3+M^-1) < Card(Omega)/Card(Omega1) <= log2(3+m^-1), where M=max Omega, m=min Omega. In fact, a sharper right inequality holds: Card(Omega)/Card(Omega1) <= log2(3+mu), where mu = (1/Card Omega1) * sum_{n in Omega1} n^-1.
explicit_conditions: Omega is a cycle of T (not necessarily nontrivial)

claims.statement_verbatim: Let p/q < p'/q' be a Farey pair. Then any intermediate fraction p/q < x/y < p'/q' with y>0 is of the form x/y = (ap+bp')/(aq+bq') where a,b are positive integers. In particular, x >= p+p' and y >= q+q'.
Let Omega be a cycle of T, and let Omega1 subset Omega denote the subset of its odd elements. Then Card Omega >= K(min Omega), Card Omega1 >= L(min Omega).
explicit_conditions: Omega is a cycle of T
claims.conclusion: Card Omega >= K(min Omega) and Card Omega1 >= L(min Omega)

claims.statement_verbatim: Let theta > 0 be irrational, theta' any number with theta < theta' < [theta]+1. If k,l are positive integers with theta < k/l <= theta', and either k or l is minimal for this property, then k/l is one of the upper convergents to theta -- precisely, the largest upper convergent <= theta'.
claims.conclusion: k/l is an upper convergent to theta (used to characterize K(m), L(m) as specific convergents, enabling their computation via Table 1/2)
